items.text: Every adult should have an equal say in the decisions that govern their society.
items.rationale: Core equal-franchise view shared by liberal, social and direct democrats and anarchists; epistocrats, monarchists and vanguardists disagree. Here-and-now answers can differ where the franchise or its weight is unequal.

items.text: Anyone should be free to form a political party and compete for power against those in charge.
items.rationale: Open political competition (including for radical or unpopular parties) is the democratic answer to one-party rule; 'anyone' makes it strong, since militant-democracy advocates would hedge. Readable in both frames.

items.text: If a decision will deeply affect people's lives, those people should have a direct say in it.
items.rationale: Participatory/affected-interests principle endorsed by participatory democrats, anarchists and localists; condition favours the Democratic pole. Frames may diverge where people judge their own country's processes unready.

items.text: Ordinary people should be able to force a public vote on any law by gathering enough signatures.
items.rationale: Citizen-initiated referendum on 'any law' is a strong participation claim (direct democrats, populists); representative democrats may answer differently per frame. Mirrors dem-09.

items.text: If one group has held power for a long time, it should have to face real rivals in a fair vote.
items.rationale: Anti-entrenchment condition favouring the Democratic pole; a sincere one-party or dynastic advocate would disagree. Works in both frames; mirrors dem-14.

items.text: If experts and the public disagree about a major policy, the public's view should win.
items.rationale: Strong popular-sovereignty stance (populists, radical democrats) opposed by technocrats; direct mirror of dem-08/dem-10. Likely to split across frames depending on trust in local experts vs local voters.

items.text: Ordinary people should be able to remove any leader at any time through a recall vote.
items.rationale: Recall 'at any time' is a strong contestability claim (council communists, direct democrats, some populists); fixed-term representative democrats may hedge. Readable in both frames.

items.text: Decisions on complex matters like the economy or public health should be made by qualified experts rather than by voters or politicians.
items.rationale: Mainstream technocratic view (expert-run agencies, meritocratic governance) a sincere technocrat endorses; democrats prefer accountable decision-makers. Frames diverge with trust in local experts.

items.text: The right to vote should depend on showing a basic understanding of how government and policy work.
items.rationale: Epistocratic restricted franchise (as defended by some political philosophers and classical republicans); strong participation limit. Mirrors dem-01 and dem-04.

items.text: If most voters know little about an issue, the decision should be left to those who have studied it.
items.rationale: Condition favouring the Hierarchical pole; technocrats, Confucian meritocrats and clerical-scholarly traditions endorse it. Here-and-now answers depend on how informed one's own electorate seems.

items.text: If a goal will take generations to reach, it should be steered by a small, stable leadership rather than by whoever wins elections.
items.rationale: Long-horizon argument used by vanguardists, developmental-state advocates and monarchists; strong because it displaces elections entirely for such goals. Mirrors dem-06.

items.text: A country is best led by a hereditary ruler who holds real power, not merely a ceremonial role.
items.note: Hereditary: passed down within a family.
items.rationale: Sincere absolute/executive monarchist position; the 'real power' clause keeps constitutional-monarchy democrats on the Democratic side (avoiding the MIT conflation). Readable in both frames, including republics.

items.text: One party or movement with a clear long-term vision should lead the country, without rival parties competing for power.
items.rationale: Vanguardist and some nationalist one-party view stated as adherents would put it; direct mirror of dem-02. Works in both frames.

items.text: If frequent elections keep disrupting long-term plans, leaders should have to face voters only rarely.
items.rationale: Condition favouring the Hierarchical pole; a moderate reduction in contestability endorsed by developmentalists and stability-first conservatives. Mirrors dem-05; frames may diverge with local electoral volatility.
